title: Tinghala chili (Tingala): Characteristics
metaDescription: Tinghala chili is an open pollinated chili variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Tinghala chili is an open pollinated chili variety, also sold or known as Tingala or Tinghala hot pepper. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor brand).

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Tinghala chili is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Tingala or Tinghala hot pepper, this is the same chili. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [chili variety finder](/crop-varieties/chili), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit chili fields most often: [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 75 to 80 days after transplanting.
**Fruit:** Labuyo type: upright fruits about 5 cm long and 5.6 g, light green turning red.
Intermediate resistance to pests and leaf diseases (seller's claim).

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: allied's open pollinated labuyo, an Allied sales manager cited it in Agriculture Monthly as a local variety of about 120,000 Scoville units. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual chili on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Tinghala chili

Decide first between siling haba, the long green finger chili for cooking, and siling labuyo, the small hot one. Hybrids bear more and for longer, while open pollinated labuyo keeps its heat and lets you save seed. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Tingala the same as Tinghala?
items.a: Yes. Tingala is another name for Tinghala. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Tinghala?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
